summary.headline: J&K Bank Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR424 crore on margin compression to 3.28% and higher standard-asset provisions, despite 25.44% advances growth.
summary.overview:
Advances grew 25.44% YoY and deposits 16.75% YoY, with both up over 4% QoQ, and the bank crossed INR3 trillion business. Operating profit was INR703 crore (+5% YoY), but net profit of INR424 crore was below last year, driven by standard-asset provisions raised on strong credit growth and lower technical write-off recoveries. NIM compressed to 3.28% as cost of deposits stayed high (4.74%) while yield on advances was 8.56%. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged for now, to be reassessed after Q2, but indicated credit growth of 18-20% against the 12% guidance.</overview>

segments.name: Retail banking
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew double digit YoY; J&K personal loans +12%, car loans +20% bank-level and +30% in ROI; agriculture +18%. Retail segment profit fell from INR472 crore in Q4 to INR196 crore, which management attributed to technical write-off recoveries booked in Q4.

segments.name: Rest of India (ROI)
segments.commentary: ROI contributes around 26% of business as on 30 June 2026, versus less than 20% a year ago. Corporate lending in ROI at competitive rates drove the quarter's growth.

segments.name: J&K and Ladakh
segments.commentary: Home-market share of banking business at 61.13% (31 March 2026); deposit market share improved in 19 of 22 districts during FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance kept unchanged for now, to be reassessed only after Q2 results: credit growth ~12%, deposit growth ~10%, CASA ~45%, NIM ~3.5%, ROA around FY26 levels, ROE ~16%, GNPA below 2.25%.
Chairman-level view: actual credit growth 'will not be less than' 18-20% in FY27; J&K growth ~12-13%, ROI growth ~25%.
ROA of 1.25%+ guided for FY27, with management saying it should show from Q2; Q1 ROA was ~0.90%.
NIM expected to return to around 3.5% 'by end of Q3, definitely'; retail yields to be at least 200 bps above corporate book.
Management expects FY27 profit to exceed FY26 profit of about INR2,367 crore.
Expects written-off recoveries of around INR250 crore (possibly INR300 crore) this year, continuing for at least FY27-FY28.
Operating expenses expected flat at worst; Q1 employee cost to be the base for the year, with some recruitment planned.
Expects retail advances growth of 55-60% in FY27 (as stated), with retail growth to exceed corporate growth by year-end.
Expects CASA ratio to improve substantially by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Plans to add 15-20 branches a year in J&K and 50-70 branches in Rest of India over the next two years.
Recruiting around 300 people for Rest of India; about 100 already posted.
INR1,250 crore capital raise approved but management is considering revising the quantum upward, which would need fresh approval; government may dilute its stake.
ECL impact on net worth: management says it should be slightly lower than the previously quantified INR1,600-1,700 crore; ECL model not yet finalised.
Possible one-off gain from sale of stake in MetLife; timing and use not decided, awaiting clearances.
demand_pricing: Corporate credit growth outpaced retail in Q1 as higher bond yields pushed companies back to bank credit; bank chose selective lending to well-rated corporates at competitive rates.
Loans to financial-market players were largely repo-linked and short-term; management says short-term lending has been avoided for ~12 months and some low-yield loans mature in the coming months.
Bulk deposits rose by about INR6,700 crore in Q1 at higher cost; management says these will be shed starting July.
Term deposits grew over 24% YoY versus CASA ~7.5%; savings balances shifted into the 888-day term deposit scheme after state government terminal-benefit receipts; 888-day rate raised 5 bps.
Salary-account MOUs signed: J&K Police, and three corporate MOUs in July covering 500-1,500 employees each; renewal of 5-year state government MOU in process.
Nearly two-thirds of industry bank credit now below 9% yield per RBI data, versus ~44% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Retail segment profit drop from INR472 crore in Q4 to INR196 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 included technical write-off recoveries booked under retail; recoveries expected in pipeline did not materialise in Q1 and are expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term credit growth outlook, split J&K vs ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Actual credit growth expected not less than 18-20% in FY27, with J&K ~12-13% and ROI ~25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins drop sharply and how will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to competitive corporate lending in ROI funded by higher-cost bulk deposits; expects NIM to reach ~3.5% by end-Q3 as bulk deposits run off and retail (higher yield) grows; calls Q1 an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected recovery from written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR250 crore expected, possibly INR300 crore; Q1 FY26 had INR70-80 crore; expected to continue for at least FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact and capital raise status?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL impact expected slightly lower than INR1,600-1,700 crore; INR1,250 crore raise approved but quantum may be revised upward; government may dilute.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise to about INR650 crore in Q1 from INR509 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 included a reversal of excess terminal-benefit provisions; Q1 includes annual provisioning of about INR150 crore for gratuity, pension and leave; Q1 expected to be the base, with slight decline before next recruitment.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans to improve CASA ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: A GM-headed CASA vertical, salary-account MOUs, transaction banking; expects substantial CASA improvement by end-Q3 FY27.
